entry.title: Larissa Fassler in conversation with Nicole Burisch

media:group.media:title: Larissa Fassler in conversation with Nicole Burisch
media:group.media:description:
Moderated by Nicole Burisch, join us for a conversation around the conclusion of the research residency of Berlin-based artist Larissa Fassler. Since September, Fassler has been conducting on-site research, worked in Concordia’s archives, and explored Montréal as she developed a new drawing that maps the university’s architecture alongside the city’s student and political movements.
About the Speaker:
• Larissa Fassler Larissa Fassler (b. 1975, Vancouver) is a Berlin-based artist whose drawings, paintings, and sculptures map the emotional, political, and physical contours of urban life. Trained at Concordia University (BFA) and Goldsmiths, University of London (MFA), she walks and measures sites using her own body before translating fieldwork, overheard conversations and signage, and archival research into dense hand-drawn compositions that expose how power and memory shape public space. Solo exhibitions include the Musée d’Orsay (Paris); Kunsthalle Lingen (Germany); the Currier Museum of Art (Manchester, New Hampshire); the Esker Foundation (Calgary); and the Canadian Cultural Centre (Paris). Group shows include the Chicago Architecture Biennial and the São Paulo Architecture Biennial. Her work is held in the National Gallery of Canada, the Berlin State Museum, FRAC Nouvelle-Aquitaine MÉCA, and the Deutsche Bank Collection. Featured in Artforum, Frieze, Canadian Art, and The New York Times; monograph published by DISTANZ (2022). Represented by Galerie Poggi, Paris.
This event was organized by Prakash Krishnan

entry.title: The Art and Science of Biodiversity

media:group.media:title: The Art and Science of Biodiversity
media:group.media:description:
Join us as Dr. Madhur Anand, ecology professor at the University of Guelph, poet, and member of the QCBS Scientific Advisory Board present an overview of her writing and leadership at the interface of art and environmental science via the University of Guelph’s “Collaboratory.”
Speakers
• Dr. Madhur Anand Madhur Anand's debut book of creative non-fiction This Red Line Goes Straight to Your Heart (2020) won the Governor General's Literary Award for Nonfiction. Her debut collection of poems A New Index for Predicting Catastrophes (2015) was a finalist for the Trillium Book Award for Poetry and named one of 10 all-time "trailblazing" poetry collections by the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation. Her second collection of poems Parasitic Oscillations (2022) was also a finalist for the Trillium Book Award for Poetry and named a Globe and Mail Top 100 Book. To Place a Rabbit, her first novel was also named a Globe and Mail Top 100 Book. Anand is a professor and the director of the Global Ecological Change and Sustainability Laboratory at the University of Guelph, Ontario.
• Dr. Carly Ziter Carly leads the Ziter Urban Landscape Ecology Lab. With her students, she uses field observations, environmental sensors, and participatory and arts-based methodologies to explore how the ways we build our cities influences biodiversity, wellbeing, and human-nature relationships. Work in the lab is done in collaboration with landowners, community groups, and local through federal governments. Carly believes strongly in science communication as an integral part of the scientific process, and has won Concordia’s research communicator of the year award at the local, national, and international levels.

entry.title: Keep the World Playing: Preserving and accessing film and video collections

media:group.media:title: Keep the World Playing: Preserving and accessing film and video collections
media:group.media:description:
On the occasion of World Audiovisual Heritage Day, we are bringing together voices from the Cinémathèque québécoise and Concordia University to explore the challenges of preserving and accessing film and video collections. This year, we will explore stories of collaboration that lead to the preservation and access of audiovisual heritage.
The event is a series of short presentations by specialists from both institutions. To broaden the conversation, the main program will be followed by a series of lightning talks, followed by a public discussion.
Speakers
• Hélène Brousseau Digital Media and Visual Resources Librarian, Concordia Library. In her presentation, Brousseau will introduce the new Guidelines for Audiovisual Resources in Libraries and Other Institutions, which were updated and approved in 2026 by the International Federation of Library Associations and Institutions (IFLA).
• Élisabeth Meunier Directrice de la préservation et du développement des collections, Cinémathèque québécoise. In her presentation: La coopération internationale : une solution pour assurer la sauvegarde du patrimoine audiovisuel (presentation in French), Meunier will report on an international cooperation project aimed at preserving and showcasing the original footage shot by filmmakers Danièle Lacourse and Yvan Patry and their team in Eritrea, Ethiopia, and Rwanda between 1985 and 1996.
• Alexandre Pagé Archival Film Projectionist (16mm IMAX 15/70mm), Concordia University. In To Screen or Not to Screen, Pagé will explore the siamese relationship of screening and preserving archival celluloid prints; the steps (and missteps) taken from inspection to projection. Using recent examples, Pagé highlights the solidarity and intricate collaborative efforts within the film archives community in Montreal.
• Tatiana Povoroznyuk Video Archive Coordinator, Community University Television - Concordia (CUTV). Since 1969, CUTV has documented arts, activism, and student life in Tiohtià:ke / Montreal. The resulting video archive consists of 1000+ magnetic tapes holding newscasts, coverage of local music, student films, and more. Povoroznyuk’s presentation CUTV Archives: Community of Stewards will tell the story of this collection, describing past and present collaborations behind the current project of digitizing and providing access to the video tapes.
Lightning Talks:
Tyisha Murphy Doctoral candidate at Concordia University, will introduce the David Webb collection.
Louis Pelletier Laboratoire CinéMédias, Université de Montréal. Pelletier will explore Elsie Reford's lenticular films.

entry.title: CTRL + AI: Creative Agency at Play

media:group.media:title: CTRL + AI: Creative Agency at Play
media:group.media:description:
Drawing from creative coding, game-making, local open-source models, and agentic workflows, Thomas Gauthier-Caron and Christian Beltrami explore new ways of closing the gap between imagination and execution while preserving human agency, authorship, and judgment. Together, they examine how experimentation and even technical failure can open unexpected creative possibilities.
AI can move an idea across words, images, code, animation, and playable systems. But as agents gain the ability not only to generate, but also to use tools and test what they create, how can humans remain active in shaping the process?
This event is presented as part of the 8th ELEKTRA Digital Art Biennale, “F(R)ICTION: Art and Games”, taking place from October 15 to November 15, 2026.

media:group.media:title: Inside Grad Life at Concordia
media:group.media:description:
What is graduate student life really like at Concordia?
In this student-led panel, Concordia Graduate Student Ambassadors will share an inside look at their academic, research, social and professional experiences. From coursework and research to building community, finding support and managing a busy schedule, this session will help you better understand what life as a graduate student can look like.
Whether you are considering a course-based program, a research degree, or are still exploring your options, this session will give you practical advice and real student perspectives to help you picture your next step.

media:group.media:title: Concordia University Press: 10th Anniversary Celebration
media:group.media:description:
October 2026 marks the tenth anniversary of the launch of Concordia University Press, the peer-reviewed and open-access book publisher based in the Concordia University Library. As part of International Open Access Week, come celebrate ten years of barrier-free scholarship and award-winning book design.
Please join us for a reception and showcase of books, remarks of thanks and reminiscence, and a chance to mingle with authors, colleagues, readers, and supporters.

entry.title: Barry Eidlin, Solidarity is the New Collegiality

media:group.media:title: Barry Eidlin, Solidarity is the New Collegiality
media:group.media:description:
In this talk, professor and longtime labour activist Barry Eidlin assesses the challenges currently facing faculty and teaching staff in Quebec and across Canada, and discusses concrete steps being taken to confront those challenges.
Across Canada, university faculty and teaching staff are facing similar challenges: budget cuts, hiring freezes, declining administrative and teaching support, increasing precarity and service obligations, eroding salaries and benefits, attacks on academic freedom, and more. Meanwhile, the ranks of administrators continue to grow, along with their salaries and the number of strategic initiatives promising to “modernize” or “realign” the university’s mission for the 21st century—often by remodeling the university along corporate lines. In response, faculty and teaching staff have been fighting back, often through collective action. But recent attacks on unions and collective bargaining at the provincial and federal levels are threatening to limit our ability to push for our vision of what the modern university can and should be.

entry.title: Oral History Off the Record: Podcast Launch

media:group.media:title: Oral History Off the Record: Podcast Launch
media:group.media:description:
Join us for the launch of Oral History Off the Record, a new podcast by the Kitchen Table Collective (KTC). Once a month, hosts Cassandra Marsillo and Hana Sherafati Zanganeh interview practitioners from around the world to understand what goes into asking the important questions: What can we learn from oral historians and their expertise in listening? And why do we believe that oral history can save the world? At this launch and special live episode recording, hear from members of the KTC as they reflect on what it means to be doing oral history in this moment and the value of listening in an age of polycrisis.
The panel will be followed by a catered lunch. Free to attend in person or virtually.
The Kitchen Table Collective is an online network founded by Stacey Zembrzycki and Anna Sheftel in September 2023, which brings together an international and intergenerational group of oral historians to discuss developments in the field, and how we are collectively navigating the politics of our institutions, communities, and everyday lives.

media:group.media:title: Women Leading Sustainability
media:group.media:description:
Join us for a screening of a three-part video interview series featuring three BIPOC women-owned small businesses in Montreal that prioritize sustainability in their work and projects. Following the 30-minute screening, we’ll have a Q&A with the featured women hosted by the director of photography. The series celebrates local entrepreneurs, highlights sustainable business practices, and encourages more environmentally conscious choices.
Speakers
• Ahana B. Murumbi Ahana B. Murumbi is a Congolese-Canadian writer, director, and producer based in Montreal. Through AYORHA Productions, she creates intimate, character-driven films exploring displacement, identity, resilience, and the human condition. Her work has earned international recognition, with her short documentary A Girl Named Abigaël (2024) named a Best Social Awareness finalist in South Africa and nominated for Best First-Time Filmmaker at Venice Shorts in Los Angeles. In 2025, she was selected as one of 17 filmmakers for Telefilm Canada’s Talent to Watch program to develop her debut feature documentary, The Shadows of the Metropolis, which has received support from Telefilm Canada and the Canada Council for the Arts.
• Eva Kyne Eva Kyne is a Canadian filmmaker, editor, and Concordia University alumna in Communications. Since 2022, she has led communications and event management at CEED Concordia, supporting the organization’s programming, outreach, and community initiatives. Her work has included teaching video production workshops to students in Uganda and, since2024, managing the CEED Concordia office and monthly markets that support BIPOC entrepreneurs.
• Kiana Picanco Kiana Picanco is a Montreal-based filmmaker and cinematographer whose work explores women and representation through visual storytelling. She holds a Bachelor’s degree with a Specialization in Communication Studies and a Minor in Film Studies from Concordia University, where she also recently completed her Master of Fine Arts in Cinematic Arts. Her work spans cinematography, editing, and scriptwriting, with a particular interest in creating complex and dynamic female characters. Her MFA research-creation project focused on plus-size representation in cinema and resulted primarily in a short horror film. She hopes to continue developing stories that challenge stereotypes surrounding women in film, particularly the representation of plus-size women.
• Clara Olivia Levesque Clara Olivia Levesque (elle/she/her) is a multidisciplinary Indian-Québécois artist working from an ecofeminist lens. She mainly illustrates figurative nymphs and incorporates them with fauna and flora to draw parallels on how interconnected we are and encourage sustainable practices with the land and between human beings. She graduated in 2025 from Concordia in Psychology and is now pursuing her studies in Art Therapy at UQAT. She is an artist that creates her artworks on her own upcycled chai paper and has recently started making her own frames using sustainable practices. She is also a vocal advocate on gender-based violence and uses her artmaking to foster discussion and meaningful change on how creative practice, intersectional and trauma-informed feminism, sustainability, gender advocacy and social justice all intersect.

entry.title: Reinventing Photography: Originary Moments and Primal Scenes (B)

media:group.media:title: Reinventing Photography: Originary Moments and Primal Scenes (B)
media:group.media:description:
The French Ministère de la culture, in association with a scientific committee of scholars, curators, and artists, has officially designated 2026/2027 as the Bicentennial of Photography, marking the moment that Nicéphore Niépce succeeded in preserving the fleeting image formed by a camera obscura on a tin plate. A year of celebration includes exhibitions, publications, conferences, and commissions that mark the invention, while continuing to probe the nature of the medium, the effect and affect of practice and preservation, and its relevance today. Let us play.
This session has been conceived as a constellation of short papers, demonstrations, and performances reflecting on an image (mental or material) that flashed up before the presenter, and continues to do so, as an inspiration or counter-inspiration for their work. The image need not come from any artistic canon or scientific discovery, though it might. Perhaps the speaker took such an image; perhaps they recognized it in an album, an archive or a flea market; perhaps it never existed (ekphrasis welcome!). This exercise need not be confessional or sentimental, though passion, from crazy love to righteous anger, is to be expected.
In the interdisciplinary spirit of photography studies and the intermediation of contemporary art, and with the current upsurge in interest in the archival practices, possibilities are limitless. No geographical or temporal boundaries could or should be imposed. For both speakers and attendees, this double session will be an opportunity to workshop ideas. We are testing the waters for the contents of a special issue or book that will reveal the wellsprings, interests and audacity of current photography research and creative practice.
